quests.instruction: Choose the clearest way to say this.
quests.scene: At a restaurant, you have a nut allergy and the waiter asks if you're ready to order.
options: Nothing with nuts in it, please, or I'll be in real trouble later tonight, and so will you.
I'm allergic to nuts, so I'll just have the salad with no sauce.
Is the chef careful? I don't want to be ill like I was last time.
I have a nut allergy. Could you check whether the sauce contains any?
quests.hint: State the allergy and ask a checkable question.
quests.explanation: Naming the allergy and asking a specific check gives the waiter something to verify. Vague warnings, avoiding the question, or general worries don't confirm whether the dish is safe.
quests.culturalNote: Restaurants usually take allergy statements seriously, and clear wording helps staff pass it to the kitchen accurately.

quests.scene: You paid with a ten, but the cashier gives you change for a twenty. You notice as you count it.
options: Thanks!
I think there's a small error, but I'm sure it evens out over the day, so don't worry about the till.
Excuse me, I think you gave me change for a twenty, but I paid with a ten.
You've made a mistake with my change. Please check it properly.
quests.hint: Point to the exact mismatch, calmly.
quests.explanation: Stating the specific discrepancy lets the cashier fix it without embarrassment. Silence keeps money that isn't yours, and vague or scolding remarks make it awkward.
quests.culturalNote: Cashiers are often held responsible for till shortfalls, so speaking up is genuinely helpful to them.

quests.scene: After a group meal, the waiter asks how you'd like to pay. You only had a salad and a glass of water.
options: Just give me the total and I'll pay what I owe.
We'd better split it evenly, it's easier for everyone.
Could we split the bill so I only pay for my own dishes?
I only had a salad, so I'm paying much less than the others.
quests.hint: Suggest a method that is fair and easy for the waiter.
quests.explanation: Asking for itemized payment is clear and fair. Vague total requests, an even split you don't agree with, or announcing your low share make it harder or awkward.
quests.culturalNote: Itemized splitting is common among friends in some countries; in others, an even split is the norm, so it helps to ask early.

quests.scene: At a pharmacy, you ask for cold medicine. You take blood pressure tablets every day.
options: I'm taking blood pressure tablets. Is this cold medicine safe to take with them?
What's good for a cold? I'm fine with anything they have in stock.
Which cold medicine works best? I need something strong today.
I'll take this one; I usually just take whatever's on offer at the shop, and it's never caused me any problems before.
quests.hint: Give the pharmacist the information that matters.
quests.explanation: Mentioning your medication invites a safety check. General questions leave out the interaction risk.
quests.culturalNote: Pharmacists in many English-speaking countries expect to be asked about interactions, and it's a routine part of their job.

quests.instruction: Pick the best way to handle this.
quests.scene: You want to return a jacket you bought last week, but you lost the receipt.
options: I'd like a refund. I don't have a receipt, but it's faulty.
I bought this last week but I've lost the receipt. Could you look it up with my card or exchange it?
I don't have the receipt, but you must remember me, I was here Monday.
Your refund policy is unreasonable. Everyone loses receipts sometimes, and I've spent a lot of money in this shop over the years.
quests.hint: Say what's missing and propose alternatives.
quests.explanation: Admitting the missing receipt and offering ways to verify gives the shop a solution. Inventing a fault or criticizing policy makes it harder.
quests.culturalNote: Return policies vary by shop, and many can check a card payment even without a receipt.

quests.scene: Your hotel room is next to a noisy stairwell and you couldn't sleep last night.
options: This room is terrible. I can't sleep at all with all this noise.
I'd like a discount for the noise, please, since it ruined my night and I'm paying a lot for this room.
Can you tell the guests upstairs to be quiet? It's every night.
The room above us is quite noisy. Would it be possible to move to a quieter one?
quests.hint: Ask for the fix you want, not just a complaint.
quests.explanation: A polite request for a specific solution gives reception something concrete. Complaints or demands for discounts are less likely to produce a room change.
quests.culturalNote: Hotels usually try to move guests if a quieter room is available; asking early works best.

quests.scene: In a taxi, the driver takes a route that seems much longer than the one on your phone map.
options: You're taking me the long way, aren't you? I'm not paying extra for a detour that you chose to take.
Stop the car. I'll get out here and walk the rest of the way.
It's fine, I'm not in a hurry, take whichever route you like.
Excuse me, is this the fastest route? My map shows another road.
quests.hint: Ask a question; don't accuse.
quests.explanation: A neutral question lets the driver explain (roadworks, traffic) or change course. Accusations or walking away escalate; silence accepts a possible overcharge.
quests.culturalNote: Drivers sometimes avoid a route for good reasons such as traffic, so asking rather than accusing keeps it friendly.

quests.scene: A food delivery arrived cold and forty minutes late. You're writing to customer support.
options: Your service is awful. I want a full refund immediately, please.
My order arrived cold and forty minutes late. Could I have a partial refund?
My food was cold, so I'm giving you one star on your app.
Everything arrived cold, but I'm not really that bothered about it, so I don't need any kind of refund.
quests.hint: State the facts and a proportionate request.
quests.explanation: Concrete facts with a reasonable request are easy for support to grant. Angry demands, threats, or shrugging don't produce a fair resolution.
quests.culturalNote: Support teams often have set refund options, so a specific, reasonable request is more likely to succeed.

quests.scene: A mechanic's final quote is much higher than the estimate he gave you last week.
options: That's a rip-off. I'll take my car somewhere else instead.
Go ahead and do it, I suppose I don't really have a choice now that the car is already in pieces in your garage.
The quote is higher than the estimate you gave me. Could you explain the difference?
You promised me a lower price, so I won't pay any more.
quests.hint: Ask for the reason before deciding.
quests.explanation: Asking for an explanation may reveal a legitimate cost or an error. Accusing or giving in prevents a fair resolution.
quests.culturalNote: In many places, garages are expected to get approval before exceeding an estimate.

quests.instruction: Choose the best response as a waiter.
quests.scene: A customer says her steak is overcooked. You want her to leave satisfied.
options: It's cooked the way the menu describes it, but I can ask the chef to look at it if you really think it's wrong.
Sorry, we're very busy tonight, so a new one will take a while.
Would you like a different dish, or perhaps a discount instead?
I'm sorry about that — let me take it back and have the kitchen make a fresh one right away.
quests.hint: Fix the problem first; discuss policy later.
quests.explanation: Apologizing and offering an immediate remedy makes her feel heard. Defending the dish, warning about delays, or negotiating alternatives put the burden back on her.
quests.culturalNote: In service work, quick remedies usually matter more than debates about who is right.

quests.scene: You work in customer support. A customer is angry about a billing error you can't correct yourself.
options: I understand why that's frustrating. I can't change the charge myself, but I'll escalate it today and call you back by five.
I'm sorry, there's nothing I can do about billing on my end.
Calm down, sir, I'm trying to help you with this here.
I'll pass it to the billing team, and they'll deal with it eventually.
quests.hint: Be honest about limits and commit to a next step.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging feelings, stating your limit, and giving a timeframe builds trust. Shutting the door, telling someone to calm down, or vague promises worsen frustration.
quests.culturalNote: 'Calm down' is widely heard as dismissive in English-speaking customer service.

quests.scene: You're a receptionist and a patient asks for a doctor's appointment. There's nothing available for two weeks.
options: We're fully booked. Try again next week and see if there's anything.
I'm afraid there's nothing available at the moment, sorry about that.
You'll have to book online, I can't help you over the phone.
The next available appointment is on the 12th. I can add you to a cancellation list, if you'd like.
quests.hint: Give the truth, then offer what you can do.
quests.explanation: Stating the earliest date and an alternative gives the patient options. A bare no or a redirect leaves them stuck.
quests.culturalNote: Cancellation lists are common in clinics and can shorten waits.

quests.scene: At a station ticket window, you want to go to Oxford and back today and would like the cheapest option.
options: What ticket should I buy for Oxford?
I need to go to Oxford and back today. What's the cheapest ticket for that?
Give me a ticket to Oxford, whichever is cheapest.
How much is it to go to Oxford? It's probably expensive, so I might just drive there instead if it's too much.
quests.hint: Give the details that let the clerk choose for you.
quests.explanation: Naming the return trip, date, and your goal lets the clerk find the best fare. Vague or incomplete questions may produce a more expensive ticket.
quests.culturalNote: Rail fares often differ by time and return type, so details matter.

quests.scene: You've lost your debit card and are calling your bank.
options: I've lost my debit card and need to block it right away. Could you help me do that?
My card is gone. Someone must have stolen it, I think, because I had it in my coat pocket on the train earlier.
I can't find my card. Can you send me a new one?
I lost my card somewhere. It might turn up, though.
quests.hint: State what you want done first.
quests.explanation: Asking to block the card immediately protects your money. Speculating about theft or delaying the block leaves your account exposed.
quests.culturalNote: Banks usually advise blocking a missing card immediately, even if you might find it.

quests.scene: Your library book is due tomorrow but you haven't finished it.
options: Could I extend this loan for another week? I haven't finished it.
Can I keep this book longer? I'm still using it for something and I'll bring it back whenever I've finished.
I'm returning it late because I couldn't finish reading it.
I'll bring it back when I've finished, if that's fine.
quests.hint: Ask before the due date, and be specific.
quests.explanation: Asking for a specific extension before the deadline follows the library's process. Vague or after-the-fact statements can lead to fines.
quests.culturalNote: Many libraries allow renewals if nobody else has reserved the book.

quests.scene: You want to cancel your gym membership, and the staff member starts offering discounts.
options: I'll think about it and let you know, maybe next month.
That discount is tempting, but I'm not sure I'll use the gym enough to justify staying on, even at that price.
I've decided to cancel, thanks. Could you confirm the last payment date in writing?
I don't want a cheaper deal, I just want out of the contract.
quests.hint: Be firm and ask for confirmation.
quests.explanation: A clear decision plus a request for written confirmation prevents later charges. Wavering invites more sales pitches.
quests.culturalNote: Retention offers are common; a polite but firm no is normal.

quests.scene: You've been a customer of your phone company for four years and your bill has crept up.
options: Your prices are too high. Another company offered me half of this, so unless you can match it I'm leaving.
I've been with you for four years. Are there any current offers that would lower my monthly bill?
I'm going to cancel unless you give me a discount right now.
Can I have a discount? Everyone else seems to get one.
quests.hint: Use your loyalty as a reason, not a threat.
quests.explanation: Mentioning your tenure and asking about offers invites a helpful answer. Ultimatums or comparisons put the agent on the defensive.
quests.culturalNote: Loyalty deals often exist but aren't advertised, so asking politely can pay off.

quests.scene: At a restaurant, you and a friend want to talk, but the table by the entrance is loud.
options: This table is too noisy. Give us another one, please.
Is there another table? This one is right by the door.
We might leave if we can't move somewhere better.
Could we move to a quieter table? We'd like to talk.
quests.hint: Give the reason and ask, don't demand.
quests.explanation: A polite request with a reason is easy for staff to say yes to. Commands or hints of leaving feel pushy.
quests.culturalNote: Restaurants often accommodate reasonable seating requests if tables are free.

quests.scene: You're chatting with tech support because your laptop won't turn on after an update.
options: My laptop is broken. Please fix it as soon as possible.
My laptop won't turn on since the update yesterday. The charging light comes on, but the screen stays black.
Something is wrong with my laptop after the update.
It doesn't work anymore. I've tried everything I can think of.
quests.hint: Describe symptoms, timing, and what you see.
quests.explanation: Specific symptoms help the agent diagnose faster. Vague statements force extra questions.
quests.culturalNote: Clear details often shorten support conversations significantly.

quests.scene: You're writing a review of a hotel where the heating broke for two nights, but the room was clean.
options: Worst hotel ever. Avoid at all costs!
The staff were incompetent and the room was disgusting. I'd never recommend this place to anyone, ever, under any circumstances.
The room was clean, but the heating was broken for two nights and staff were slow to respond.
It was okay. Not the best, but not the worst either.
quests.hint: Be specific and fair.
quests.explanation: Balanced, concrete details help other travelers and are more credible. Extreme or vague reviews are less helpful.
quests.culturalNote: Readers tend to trust reviews that mention specifics and positives as well as negatives.

quests.scene: You're emailing a company to cancel a subscription and want proof that no further payments will be taken.
options: I want to unsubscribe. Please stop charging me.
Please cancel my subscription effective today, and confirm by email that no further payments will be taken.
Could you please consider cancelling my subscription when convenient?
I'm no longer interested in your service, so cancel it.
quests.hint: Be direct, specific about timing, and ask for confirmation.
quests.explanation: A clear instruction with confirmation request protects you. Requests or demands without confirmation risk continued billing.
quests.culturalNote: Written confirmation is a good habit for cancellations.

quests.scene: A waiter asks, 'Was everything okay?' The soup was cold but the rest was lovely.
options: Everything was perfect.
Fine.
The soup was cold. I expected better from a place like this, considering how much you charge for a starter.
Mostly good, thanks — the soup was a bit cold, but the rest was lovely.
quests.hint: Give honest, balanced feedback.
quests.explanation: A balanced answer gives useful feedback without harshness. Automatic praise hides the issue, and blunt complaints sound hostile.
quests.culturalNote: Staff usually want honest feedback when asked politely, and 'Everything was fine' can hide problems.

quests.instruction: Choose the best way to handle this.
quests.scene: At airport check-in, your bag is two kilos over the limit.
options: It's only two kilos over. Surely that doesn't matter, and the plane won't notice the difference between two kilos and none.
I'll pay the fee, but it's ridiculous.
My bag is two kilos over. Could I move a few items to my carry-on instead of paying the fee?
Can you let it go this once? I'm a frequent flyer.
quests.hint: Propose a solution within the rules.
quests.explanation: Offering to repack respects the policy and saves you money. Arguing or asking for exceptions rarely works.
quests.culturalNote: Airline baggage limits are usually strict, and repacking is common practice.

quests.scene: Your haircut is shorter than you asked for. The stylist is still holding the mirror.
options: I think it's a little shorter than we discussed. Can you tidy up the sides for me?
This isn't what I asked for. I can't go out like this, and I have an important interview first thing tomorrow morning.
It's lovely, thanks.
I'll pay, but I won't be back here again.
quests.hint: Say what's off and ask for what could help.
quests.explanation: Naming the difference and asking for a fix is constructive. Silence or angry threats offer no solution.
quests.culturalNote: Stylists usually welcome feedback while you're still in the chair.

quests.scene: At a supermarket checkout, an elderly customer is struggling with the card machine and the queue is growing.
options: Take your time. Would you like me to hold your bag while you type in the PIN?
The machine is a bit slow. Just try again in a moment.
Do you need help? Older people often struggle with these machines, so don't feel bad about being slow with it.
Please hurry, there's a queue behind you, unfortunately.
quests.hint: Offer help without making it about age.
quests.explanation: A calm, practical offer preserves dignity. Comments about age or pressure to hurry are unkind.
quests.culturalNote: Offers of help are best framed around the task, not the person's age.

quests.scene: A customer at your counter speaks limited English and is struggling to explain what she needs.
options: I'll try a simpler word. Do you understand English at all, or should I get somebody who speaks your language?
Take your time. I can speak slowly, or we can write it down.
Can you come back with someone who speaks English?
Just point to what you want and I'll guess.
quests.hint: Make it easier without making her feel bad.
quests.explanation: Offering time and options is patient and respectful. Testing her, sending her away, or guessing are less helpful.
quests.culturalNote: Patience and simple alternatives are widely appreciated by non-native speakers.

quests.scene: You left a black rucksack with a laptop on the 9:15 train to Leeds and are at the lost property desk.
options: I lost my bag on a train. It's really important to me, and I'd like someone to look for it as soon as possible, please.
Someone took my bag from the train. Please find it.
I left a black rucksack on the 9:15 to Leeds. It has my laptop inside. Can I leave my number?
Has anyone handed in a bag? It's black, I think.
quests.hint: Give the details staff need to find it.
quests.explanation: Specifics (train, item, contents) and contact details help staff match it. Vague or accusatory reports don't.
quests.culturalNote: Lost property offices match items using details, so specifics matter.

quests.scene: You reported a leaking tap to your landlord three weeks ago and nothing has happened.
options: The tap is still leaking. What am I paying rent for?
I'll get a plumber myself and send you the bill.
I reported the leaking tap three weeks ago. Could you tell me when it will be fixed?
It's not urgent, but the tap has been dripping a bit for a while now, in case you happen to be free at some point.
quests.hint: Refer to the earlier report and ask for a date.
quests.explanation: Referring to the history and asking for a date is firm and polite. Complaints or unilateral action can cause conflict.
quests.culturalNote: Tenants' rights vary by region, so it's worth checking local rules before hiring repairs yourself.

quests.scene: You're phoning a taxi firm to book a ride for your mother, who uses a wheelchair.
options: I need a taxi for eight o'clock tomorrow morning. My mother uses a wheelchair, so we need a vehicle with a ramp.
I need a taxi tomorrow at eight for two people, please.
Please send a big car tomorrow morning, we have some luggage.
Do you have any accessible taxis? I'll call back later.
quests.hint: Include the requirement that affects the booking.
quests.explanation: Mentioning the wheelchair and ramp at booking ensures the right vehicle. Omitting it risks a wasted trip.
quests.culturalNote: Accessible vehicles are often limited, so booking with details in advance helps.

quests.scene: You're phoning your insurer to report a minor car collision that happened yesterday at 5 p.m. Nobody was hurt.
options: I had a car accident, and I'd like to make a claim, please.
Someone hit my car, and it was completely their fault.
There was a bit of an accident. I'm not sure what to do.
I'd like to report a minor collision that happened yesterday at 5 p.m. No one was injured. I have photos of the damage.
quests.hint: Give the key facts in a logical order.
quests.explanation: Time, severity, injuries, and evidence help the insurer start the claim. Vague or blame-heavy statements slow things down.
quests.culturalNote: Insurers typically ask about injuries and evidence first, so leading with them saves time.
